transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess what finally made me come in is my head just doesn’t feel clear. It’s like I’m trying to do my normal work — looking at a board packet, or reading through a vendor email — and I just sit there staring at it. I used to be able to sort through those things pretty quickly, make a decision, move on to the next thing. Now even simple things feel like they take forever, and I keep thinking, “Why can’t I just decide this?”

It’s not that I don’t know the work. I’ve done this kind of thing for years. But lately it feels cloudy up there, like I’m pushing through fog, and it’s frustrating because these are things I’m supposed to handle. That’s really what brought me in.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

I’m not sure I’d call it depressed, exactly. I mean, I get upset with myself, definitely — more discouraged than anything, because I’ll sit there and think, “I should be able to do this, why is this taking me so long?” But when you say depressed, I don’t know… I guess I don’t really know where the line is between being frustrated and being down.

I wouldn’t say I came in thinking, “I’m depressed.” It’s more that something feels off, and then that makes me feel bad about myself. Like I’m not keeping up the way I normally would. So… maybe a little down at times, but I’m not sure if that’s the right word.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yes… I think I have, now that you say it that way. I didn’t really call it that in my head, but there are things I normally look forward to that I just… haven’t wanted to do.

Like my dance class — I usually like going, even if I’m tired, because once I’m there I feel better and I know the people. Lately I’ll think about getting dressed and driving over there, and I just don’t want to. And I used to like walking around and looking at the little galleries, just seeing pretty things, getting ideas, but I haven’t had the pull to do that either.

And Sundays… I usually cook for my family. Nothing fancy, just the food we’re used to, the kind that makes the house feel right. But even that has felt like too much, or like I don’t care the same way. Those things usually make me feel like myself, so it bothers me that I’m not wanting them.
For at least the past two weeks, have you been feeling down or less interested in things most of the day nearly every day?

Yes… I think so. I mean, not every single minute, but most days it’s been there in the background. The biggest thing is I just haven’t wanted to do the things I normally do, the things that usually make me feel like myself.

Like I said, I haven’t wanted to go to my dance class, and that’s strange for me because I usually enjoy it once I’m there. I haven’t felt like going to look at the little galleries either, which is something I used to do just because it made me feel good. And even cooking Sunday food for my family… that usually feels important to me, like part of who I am, and lately I just don’t have the same interest in doing it.

So yes, for the past couple of weeks or so, I’d say I’ve been less interested most of the day, most days.
Before this current period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things for two weeks or longer?

Yes… I think there have been other stretches, if I’m being honest. It’s not like this is the very first time I’ve felt this kind of heaviness or like I don’t care about things the way I usually do.

Over maybe the past year, it’s been coming and going. I’d have these periods where I’d feel down or just kind of lose my spark for a while, and then it would lift some, so I’d tell myself, “Okay, I’m fine, it passed.” But then later it would come back again.

This latest one feels a little different to me, though, or maybe more connected to what’s been going on at home. It seemed to get worse after my husband stopped working. I don’t know if that’s the cause exactly, but that’s when I noticed it more — like the whole feeling of being weighed down and not wanting to do my usual things became harder to shake. So yes, before this, there were other times, on and off, that lasted a couple weeks or longer.
Did these symptoms start after your husband stopped working?

Yes, that’s when I really noticed it getting sharper. I mean, I’d had ups and downs before, but this particular change — my energy dropping, not feeling confident in myself, and then this kind of low, cloudy feeling — it seemed to start after my husband retired and was suddenly home all day.

It’s been about two weeks now, maybe right around there. I don’t want to blame him exactly, because it’s not that simple, but the timing lines up. Once he was home all the time, the house felt different, my routine felt different, and that’s when I started feeling more weighed down.
During this current period, have you been feeling sad or depressed?

I don’t know if I’d use the word depressed exactly… sad, yes, some days. It’s more like I feel low or heavy, like I’m not quite myself. I can still get up and do what I need to do, so part of me says, “Well, maybe it’s not that bad,” but there’s definitely been this sadness sitting there.

It’s not like I’m crying all day or anything like that. It’s more quiet than that. I’ll be doing something ordinary and just feel this dull, down feeling come over me. So yes, I guess I have been feeling sad during this period, but I keep going back and forth on what to call it.
Since your husband stopped working, has this been interfering with your day-to-day functioning?

Yes… I mean, I’m still functioning, if that’s what you mean. I’m still getting myself to work, I’m not staying in bed or anything like that. But I can tell I’m not operating the way I usually do.

At work, I’ve been slowing myself down a lot more before making decisions. Normally I can look at something, sort through it, and decide what needs to be done, especially with vendors or board issues. Lately I keep second-guessing myself, like, “Did I read that right? Am I missing something?” So I’ve been asking my assistant to double-check vendor details more than I normally would, because I just don’t trust my judgment right now.

And there are a couple of board items I’ve put off, not because they’re impossible, but because I feel like if I make the call right now, I might make the wrong one. So yes, it is interfering some. Not to the point that everything has fallen apart, but enough that I notice I’m not doing my job with the same confidence or speed.
Have you been feeling especially worried or anxious lately?

I’m not sure I’d say especially anxious. I mean, I do worry, but I’ve always been someone who thinks things through, maybe too much sometimes. Lately I notice myself turning things over in my head more, but I don’t know if that’s anxiety exactly or just me not feeling as steady as I usually do.

It’s not like I’m sitting there panicking, if that’s what you mean. It’s more… I’ll pause and think, “Am I handling this right?” or “Should I check that again?” But I wouldn’t say I feel scared all the time or anything that strong. So I guess my answer is, maybe a little worried, but I’m not sure I’d call it especially anxious.
Before your husband retired, was there ever a time when you felt this same kind of low mood or loss of interest nearly every day for two weeks or longer?

Yes… before he stopped working, I think there were times like that, though I’m not sure I was naming it that way at the time. It’s been kind of coming and going for maybe about a year now, these stretches where I feel low and sort of pulled back from things, not just for a day here or there.

Some of those periods did last a couple of weeks, I think. It’s not always dramatic, so I can talk myself out of calling it anything serious, but looking back, yes, there were stretches where it was there nearly every day.

This latest one feels more connected to my husband not working anymore, like that change stirred it up or made it more noticeable. But the low patches themselves didn’t start only after that. They’ve been on and off before then.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

I’m not really sure how to answer that, because I haven’t been tracking it closely. I don’t think I’ve noticed a major problem, like something obvious where I’d say, “Oh, I’m not sleeping at all,” or anything like that.

Some nights I might wake up or not feel completely rested, but I don’t know if that’s unusual for me or just normal at my age, or because I’m thinking about things before bed. I wouldn’t say sleep is the main thing I’ve been concerned about. If you mean trouble falling asleep every night or being up for hours, I don’t think so… at least not that I’ve really noticed.
Have you been having trouble with your memory?

Memory… I don’t know if I’d call it memory exactly, like forgetting people’s names or not knowing where I am. It’s more that my head feels cloudy. That’s actually a lot of why I came in.

I’ll be looking at a board packet, or a vendor email, something I used to go through pretty quickly, and I just sort of stare at it. I read the same part again and again, and then I still can’t seem to decide what to do with it. Even simple things, like whether something needs a call back or whether I should approve a small thing, feel harder than they should.

It makes me feel foolish, honestly, because these are things I’ve handled for years. It’s not that I don’t know how, exactly. It’s like the thinking part is slow or foggy, and I can’t get myself to land on an answer. So if that counts as memory trouble, then yes, but to me it feels more like trouble thinking clearly.
Have you been forgetting recent conversations or appointments?

I don’t think so… not in the way you mean, I don’t think. I haven’t been missing appointments, at least not that I can remember, and I don’t have people telling me, “We already talked about this,” or anything like that.

Sometimes I’ll second-guess myself, like I’ll think, did I already call that person back, or did I just mean to call them? But then if I look at my notes or my calendar, usually I can sort it out. I’ve always kept lists and written things down for work, so it’s hard to know how much is memory and how much is just me relying on my usual system.

With conversations, I might not remember every little detail, especially if I wasn’t fully focused, but I don’t think I’m forgetting whole conversations. It’s more that I feel unsure of myself and have to check things more than I used to.
Have you noticed your appetite has gone down lately?

Yes… I think it has, though it’s kind of uneven. It’s not like I never eat, but my eating has been off. A lot of days I’ll have coffee, and then maybe just a few bites of something, and somehow I just keep going like that for most of the day.

Then later at night I’ll realize I didn’t really eat properly, but even then I’m not sitting down to a real meal. I’ll just pick at something, like tortillas or something sweet, a little here and there. And I don’t even enjoy it much, which is strange for me. It’s more like I’m eating because it’s there, or because I know I should have something, not because I’m hungry.

So yes, I guess my appetite is down, or at least it doesn’t feel normal.
Lately, have you been feeling slowed down in your thinking or movements?

Yes… both, actually, which sounds a little contradictory, but that’s what it feels like.

At home, especially when I’m just going from the bedroom to the kitchen or trying to get something done around the house, I feel slow. Like my legs are heavy, almost like I’m walking through mud. I’ll think, “Just get up and do the thing,” and then even moving feels like it takes more effort than it should.

But then when I’m in meetings, it’s almost the opposite on the outside. I’ll catch myself tapping my pen, shifting around in the chair, crossing and uncrossing my legs. I feel keyed up, like I can’t quite sit still, even if I’m trying to look calm and professional. So my body feels heavy sometimes, and other times it’s restless. My thinking feels slowed down too, like I said before, but the moving part is strange because it goes both ways depending on where I am.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

I… yes, but not in the sense that I want to do something to myself. A few mornings, when I’ve first woken up, I’ve had this awful thought like, maybe it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And it scares me even saying that out loud, because I don’t want you to think I’m planning anything.

I don’t have a plan, and I don’t want to hurt myself. It’s more like a tired, heavy thought that comes over me for a minute, like not wanting to face the day. Then I feel guilty or frightened that I even thought it. So yes, the thought has been there a few times, but I’m not trying to harm myself.
Do you have any plan to hurt yourself?

No. No, I don’t have any plan to hurt myself.

That’s the part I want to be really clear about, because the thought scares me, but it isn’t like I’m thinking through a way to do anything. It’s more that a few mornings I’ve woken up and had this heavy, awful thought like, maybe it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And then I kind of get frightened by my own mind for even going there.

But I don’t want to hurt myself. I’m not planning anything. It’s just been that thought, and I don’t like that it’s there.
Between these low periods over the past year, was there ever a stretch of at least two months when you felt back to your usual self?

I’m trying to think about that carefully, because it hasn’t been one straight line the whole year. It’s more like these low stretches keep coming back on and off, and then I’ll have times where I’m functioning more like myself again, or at least I think, “Okay, maybe I’m coming out of it.”

But I don’t know that I’d say there was a clear two-month stretch where I felt fully back to normal. Maybe better here and there, yes. The latest one feels different to me, or more tied to what happened after my husband stopped working. Since then it’s felt heavier, like it has more to do with the change at home and everything around that.

So… over the past year, yes, it’s been on and off, but this current stretch is the one that feels most connected to that situation with my husband.
Do your symptoms feel much stronger than you would expect just from your husband retiring?

I’m not completely sure how to judge that, honestly. Part of me thinks, well, it makes sense I’d feel upset, because it changed the whole feeling in the house and my routine, and I didn’t expect that to affect me as much as it did.

But whether it’s “much stronger” than what someone should feel… I don’t know. I don’t really have a good measure for that. I just know it has felt heavier than I expected at times, but I also keep second-guessing myself, like maybe I’m just not handling the change well. So I guess I can’t say clearly. It feels connected to it, but I’m not sure if it’s out of proportion.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually high, energized, or unlike your normal self?

Yes… I think so. I don’t know if I would have called it “high” at the time, exactly, because it didn’t feel like I was out of control in some obvious way. But there have been days where I felt almost too bright, if that makes sense. Like I was suddenly more bold than usual.

At the association meetings, for example, I’d catch myself talking over people, jumping in before they finished, being very sure of myself. And part of me would think, “Well, maybe I’m just being efficient,” but later I’d feel a little embarrassed, because that isn’t really how I like to be with people.

And then I’d come home and snap at my husband over some tiny thing, something that probably didn’t deserve that reaction. It was like I had all this energy or sharpness in me, and it came out as being pushy in public and irritable at home. So yes, there were periods where I felt unlike my normal self that way.

target_item.name: Diminished_Thinking
target_item.manifestation: What brings me in is that my head feels cloudy, like I stare at a board packet or a vendor email and cannot decide even simple things I used to handle fast.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I am returning the chief complaint symptom code S031.

patient.answer:
Well… I guess what finally made me come in is my head just doesn’t feel clear. I used to be able to sort through those things pretty quickly, make a decision, move on to the next thing. It’s not that I don’t know the work. I’ve done this kind of thing for years. But lately it feels cloudy up there, like I’m pushing through fog, and it’s frustrating because these are things I’m supposed to handle. That’s really what brought me in.

doctor.question: Have you been feeling down or depressed?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about feeling down or depressed, but the symptom profile does not include a distinct depressed mood item.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I’d call it depressed, exactly. I mean, I get upset with myself, definitely — more discouraged than anything, because I’ll sit there and think, “I should be able to do this, why is this taking me so long?” But when you say depressed, I don’t know… I guess I don’t really know where the line is between being frustrated and being down.

I wouldn’t say I came in thinking, “I’m depressed.” It’s more that something feels off, and then that makes me feel bad about myself. Like I’m not keeping up the way I normally would. So… maybe a little down at times, but I’m not sure if that’s the right word.

patient.answer:
Yes, that’s when I really noticed it getting sharper. I mean, I’d had ups and downs before, but this particular change — my energy dropping, not feeling confident in myself, and then this kind of low, cloudy feeling — it seemed to start after my husband retired and was suddenly home all day.

It’s been about two weeks now, maybe right around there. I don’t want to blame him exactly, because it’s not that simple, but the timing lines up. Once he was home all the time, the house felt different, my routine felt different, and that’s when I started feeling more weighed down.

doctor.intent: Determine whether her current episode includes depressed mood, which is needed to distinguish a major depressive episode from an adjustment disorder with depressed mood.
doctor.question: During this current period, have you been feeling sad or depressed?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about sad or depressed mood during the current period, but the symptom profile does not include a separate depressed mood item.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d use the word depressed exactly… sad, yes, some days. It’s more like I feel low or heavy, like I’m not quite myself. I can still get up and do what I need to do, so part of me says, “Well, maybe it’s not that bad,” but there’s definitely been this sadness sitting there.

It’s not like I’m crying all day or anything like that. It’s more quiet than that. I’ll be doing something ordinary and just feel this dull, down feeling come over me. So yes, I guess I have been feeling sad during this period, but I keep going back and forth on what to call it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the episode is better explained as an adjustment disorder by establishing if the stressor has caused marked distress or impairment.
doctor.question: Since your husband stopped working, has this been interfering with your day-to-day functioning?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I am still getting to work, but I have had to slow down decisions, ask my assistant to double-check vendor details, and put off a couple of board items because I do not trust my judgment right now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the symptoms have been interfering with day-to-day functioning, which directly matches functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yes… I mean, I’m still functioning, if that’s what you mean. I’m still getting myself to work, I’m not staying in bed or anything like that. But I can tell I’m not operating the way I usually do.

At work, I’ve been slowing myself down a lot more before making decisions. Normally I can look at something, sort through it, and decide what needs to be done, especially with vendors or board issues. Lately I keep second-guessing myself, like, “Did I read that right? Am I missing something?” So I’ve been asking my assistant to double-check vendor details more than I normally would, because I just don’t trust my judgment right now.

And there are a couple of board items I’ve put off, not because they’re impossible, but because I feel like if I make the call right now, I might make the wrong one. So yes, it is interfering some. Not to the point that everything has fallen apart, but enough that I notice I’m not doing my job with the same confidence or speed.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has significant anxiety/worry, which would help distinguish adjustment disorder with anxiety/depressed mood or an anxiety disorder from a depressive episode.
doctor.question: Have you been feeling especially worried or anxious lately?

target_item.reason: The question is directly asking about worry or anxiety, but the provided symptom profile does not include an anxiety or excessive worry item.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I’d say especially anxious. I mean, I do worry, but I’ve always been someone who thinks things through, maybe too much sometimes. Lately I notice myself turning things over in my head more, but I don’t know if that’s anxiety exactly or just me not feeling as steady as I usually do.

It’s not like I’m sitting there panicking, if that’s what you mean. It’s more… I’ll pause and think, “Am I handling this right?” or “Should I check that again?” But I wouldn’t say I feel scared all the time or anything that strong. So I guess my answer is, maybe a little worried, but I’m not sure I’d call it especially anxious.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a distinct depressive episode lasting at least two weeks independent of the recent stressor, which would favor recurrent major depressive disorder over adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood.
doctor.question: Before your husband retired, was there ever a time when you felt this same kind of low mood or loss of interest nearly every day for two weeks or longer?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The depressed stretches have been coming back on and off for about a year, but this latest one feels more tied to what happened after my husband stopped working.
target_item.reason: The question asks whether similar depressive symptoms occurred before the current stressor and lasted two weeks or longer, which matches the history and duration of depressive episodes.

patient.answer:
Yes… before he stopped working, I think there were times like that, though I’m not sure I was naming it that way at the time. It’s been kind of coming and going for maybe about a year now, these stretches where I feel low and sort of pulled back from things, not just for a day here or there.

Some of those periods did last a couple of weeks, I think. It’s not always dramatic, so I can talk myself out of calling it anything serious, but looking back, yes, there were stretches where it was there nearly every day.

This latest one feels more connected to my husband not working anymore, like that change stirred it up or made it more noticeable. But the low patches themselves didn’t start only after that. They’ve been on and off before then.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has insomnia or hypersomnia as an additional depressive symptom to distinguish major depressive disorder from adjustment disorder and cognitive disorder.
doctor.question: Have you been having trouble sleeping?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about sleep disturbance, but the provided symptom profiles do not include a sleep-related item.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure how to answer that, because I haven’t been tracking it closely. I don’t think I’ve noticed a major problem, like something obvious where I’d say, “Oh, I’m not sleeping at all,” or anything like that.

Some nights I might wake up or not feel completely rested, but I don’t know if that’s unusual for me or just normal at my age, or because I’m thinking about things before bed. I wouldn’t say sleep is the main thing I’ve been concerned about. If you mean trouble falling asleep every night or being up for hours, I don’t think so… at least not that I’ve really noticed.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the reported 'cloudy' thinking reflects objective memory impairment, which would help distinguish a depressive episode/adjustment disorder from a cognitive disorder.
doctor.question: Have you been having trouble with your memory?

target_item.name: Diminished_Thinking
target_item.manifestation: What brings me in is that my head feels cloudy, like I stare at a board packet or a vendor email and cannot decide even simple things I used to handle fast.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about cognitive trouble, and this profile covers diminished thinking and concentration problems.

patient.answer:
Memory… I don’t know if I’d call it memory exactly, like forgetting people’s names or not knowing where I am. It’s more that my head feels cloudy. That’s actually a lot of why I came in.

I’ll be looking at a board packet, or a vendor email, something I used to go through pretty quickly, and I just sort of stare at it. I read the same part again and again, and then I still can’t seem to decide what to do with it. Even simple things, like whether something needs a call back or whether I should approve a small thing, feel harder than they should.

It makes me feel foolish, honestly, because these are things I’ve handled for years. It’s not that I don’t know how, exactly. It’s like the thinking part is slow or foggy, and I can’t get myself to land on an answer. So if that counts as memory trouble, then yes, but to me it feels more like trouble thinking clearly.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the cognitive complaints represent objective memory impairment suggestive of a neurocognitive disorder rather than depression-related poor concentration.
doctor.question: Have you been forgetting recent conversations or appointments?

target_item.reason: The question is specifically about memory problems such as forgetting recent conversations or appointments, but the provided symptom profile covers cloudy thinking/concentration and indecisiveness, not actual recent-memory loss.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… not in the way you mean, I don’t think. I haven’t been missing appointments, at least not that I can remember, and I don’t have people telling me, “We already talked about this,” or anything like that.

Sometimes I’ll second-guess myself, like I’ll think, did I already call that person back, or did I just mean to call them? But then if I look at my notes or my calendar, usually I can sort it out. I’ve always kept lists and written things down for work, so it’s hard to know how much is memory and how much is just me relying on my usual system.

With conversations, I might not remember every little detail, especially if I wasn’t fully focused, but I don’t think I’m forgetting whole conversations. It’s more that I feel unsure of myself and have to check things more than I used to.

doctor.intent: Determine whether decreased appetite is present as an additional major depressive episode symptom, helping distinguish recurrent major depressive disorder from adjustment disorder or nonspecific anxiety/cognitive complaints.
doctor.question: Have you noticed your appetite has gone down lately?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: My eating has been off, where coffee and a few bites carry me most of the day and then at night I pick at tortillas or sweets without really enjoying them.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about decreased appetite lately, which matches appetite or weight changes.

patient.answer:
Yes… I think it has, though it’s kind of uneven. It’s not like I never eat, but my eating has been off. A lot of days I’ll have coffee, and then maybe just a few bites of something, and somehow I just keep going like that for most of the day.

Then later at night I’ll realize I didn’t really eat properly, but even then I’m not sitting down to a real meal. I’ll just pick at something, like tortillas or something sweet, a little here and there. And I don’t even enjoy it much, which is strange for me. It’s more like I’m eating because it’s there, or because I know I should have something, not because I’m hungry.

So yes, I guess my appetite is down, or at least it doesn’t feel normal.

doctor.intent: Determine whether impaired concentration/decision-making is part of a major depressive episode rather than a primary neurocognitive disorder or nonspecific stress response by assessing psychomotor retardation/fatigue-like slowing.
doctor.question: Lately, have you been feeling slowed down in your thinking or movements?

target_item.name: Psychomotor_Changes
target_item.manifestation: At home I move slow like my legs are heavy, but in meetings I catch myself tapping my pen, shifting in the chair, and feeling too keyed up to sit still.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feeling physically or mentally slowed down, which most directly matches psychomotor slowing or changes in movement/activity.

patient.answer:
Yes… both, actually, which sounds a little contradictory, but that’s what it feels like.

At home, especially when I’m just going from the bedroom to the kitchen or trying to get something done around the house, I feel slow. Like my legs are heavy, almost like I’m walking through mud. I’ll think, “Just get up and do the thing,” and then even moving feels like it takes more effort than it should.

But then when I’m in meetings, it’s almost the opposite on the outside. I’ll catch myself tapping my pen, shifting around in the chair, crossing and uncrossing my legs. I feel keyed up, like I can’t quite sit still, even if I’m trying to look calm and professional. So my body feels heavy sometimes, and other times it’s restless. My thinking feels slowed down too, like I said before, but the moving part is strange because it goes both ways depending on where I am.

doctor.intent: Assess for suicidal ideation to help determine severity and support a major depressive episode diagnosis versus adjustment or nonspecific anxiety/cognitive causes.
doctor.question: Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

target_item.name: Death_Suicide
target_item.manifestation: A few mornings I have had the scary thought that maybe it would be easier if I just did not wake up, but I do not want to hurt myself and I have no plan.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about thoughts that life is not worth living or self-harm, which matches recurrent thoughts of death or suicidal ideation.

patient.answer:
I… yes, but not in the sense that I want to do something to myself. A few mornings, when I’ve first woken up, I’ve had this awful thought like, maybe it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And it scares me even saying that out loud, because I don’t want you to think I’m planning anything.

I don’t have a plan, and I don’t want to hurt myself. It’s more like a tired, heavy thought that comes over me for a minute, like not wanting to face the day. Then I feel guilty or frightened that I even thought it. So yes, the thought has been there a few times, but I’m not trying to harm myself.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the passive death thoughts are accompanied by suicidal intent or a plan, to assess immediate safety and clarify severity of the depressive episode.
doctor.question: Do you have any plan to hurt yourself?

target_item.name: Death_Suicide
target_item.manifestation: A few mornings I have had the scary thought that maybe it would be easier if I just did not wake up, but I do not want to hurt myself and I have no plan.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about suicidal intent or a plan to hurt myself, which falls under thoughts of death or suicidal ideation.

patient.answer:
No. No, I don’t have any plan to hurt myself.

That’s the part I want to be really clear about, because the thought scares me, but it isn’t like I’m thinking through a way to do anything. It’s more that a few mornings I’ve woken up and had this heavy, awful thought like, maybe it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And then I kind of get frightened by my own mind for even going there.

But I don’t want to hurt myself. I’m not planning anything. It’s just been that thought, and I don’t like that it’s there.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the current depressive symptoms represent a distinct major depressive episode by establishing whether there was a clearly symptom-free interval between prior similar periods, which helps separate recurrent major depressive disorder from a single episode or adjustment-related symptoms.
doctor.question: Between these low periods over the past year, was there ever a stretch of at least two months when you felt back to your usual self?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The depressed stretches have been coming back on and off for about a year, but this latest one feels more tied to what happened after my husband stopped working.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the course of the low/depressed periods over the past year and whether there were sustained intervals of feeling back to usual self.

patient.answer:
I’m trying to think about that carefully, because it hasn’t been one straight line the whole year. It’s more like these low stretches keep coming back on and off, and then I’ll have times where I’m functioning more like myself again, or at least I think, “Okay, maybe I’m coming out of it.”

But I don’t know that I’d say there was a clear two-month stretch where I felt fully back to normal. Maybe better here and there, yes. The latest one feels different to me, or more tied to what happened after my husband stopped working. Since then it’s felt heavier, like it has more to do with the change at home and everything around that.

So… over the past year, yes, it’s been on and off, but this current stretch is the one that feels most connected to that situation with my husband.

doctor.intent: Differentiate recurrent major depressive disorder from adjustment disorder by determining whether the current depressive symptoms are out of proportion to the stressor.
doctor.question: Do your symptoms feel much stronger than you would expect just from your husband retiring?

target_item.reason: The question is about whether the symptom intensity is disproportionate to the stressor of the husband retiring, which is not covered by any listed symptom profile item.

patient.answer:
I’m not completely sure how to judge that, honestly. Part of me thinks, well, it makes sense I’d feel upset, because it changed the whole feeling in the house and my routine, and I didn’t expect that to affect me as much as it did.

But whether it’s “much stronger” than what someone should feel… I don’t know. I don’t really have a good measure for that. I just know it has felt heavier than I expected at times, but I also keep second-guessing myself, like maybe I’m just not handling the change well. So I guess I can’t say clearly. It feels connected to it, but I’m not sure if it’s out of proportion.

doctor.intent: Assess whether there have been any past episodes of abnormally elevated or unusually energized mood to rule out bipolar spectrum illness and better distinguish recurrent major depression from other diagnoses.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually high, energized, or unlike your normal self?

target_item.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
target_item.manifestation: There were days when I felt almost too bright and bold, talking over people at the association meetings, and then I would snap at my husband over some small thing at home.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a past period of unusually high or energized mood, which directly matches elevated or expansive mood.

patient.answer:
Yes… I think so. I don’t know if I would have called it “high” at the time, exactly, because it didn’t feel like I was out of control in some obvious way. But there have been days where I felt almost too bright, if that makes sense. Like I was suddenly more bold than usual.

At the association meetings, for example, I’d catch myself talking over people, jumping in before they finished, being very sure of myself. And part of me would think, “Well, maybe I’m just being efficient,” but later I’d feel a little embarrassed, because that isn’t really how I like to be with people.

And then I’d come home and snap at my husband over some tiny thing, something that probably didn’t deserve that reaction. It was like I had all this energy or sharpness in me, and it came out as being pushy in public and irritable at home. So yes, there were periods where I felt unlike my normal self that way.

inference.note: Added F31.9 because this turn revealed past periods of feeling unusually energized/unlike herself with increased talkativeness, interrupting others, increased confidence, and irritability, raising concern for bipolar spectrum. Primary depressive diagnoses remain because duration/impairment and full hypomanic criteria are not yet established.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking help today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes recurrent depressive episodes over about the past year, with the current episode lasting at least 2 weeks and featuring depressed mood/sadness, markedly diminished interest, decreased appetite, psychomotor slowing/restlessness, impaired concentration/indecisiveness, and passive death wishes, with functional impairment at work. Prior episodes of at least 2 weeks occurred before the husband's retirement, arguing against a purely adjustment-related condition. Bipolar disorder was considered because of brief reports of feeling unusually energized, talkative, bold, and irritable, but the interview does not establish a distinct manic or hypomanic episode with sufficient duration or full syndrome criteria. Therefore recurrent depressive disorder, unspecified, is the best fit from the candidate list.
